title: Rigveda 5.46: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.46: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.46 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 364r-365r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.46.1 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 2, varga 28); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 364r
translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>hayo̱ na vi̱dvām̐ a̍yuji sva̱yaṁ dhu̱ri tāṁ va̍hāmi pra̱tara̍ṇīm ava̱syuva̍m | nāsyā̍ vaśmi vi̱muca̱ṁ nāvṛta̱m puna̍r vi̱dvān pa̱thaḥ pu̍rae̱ta ṛ̱ju ne̍ṣati ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>WELL knowing I have bound me, horselike, to the pole: I carry that which bears as on and gives us help. I seek for no release, no turning back therefrom. May he who knows the way, the Leader, guide me straight.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 364r (numbered 37r by the scribe) (OPenn image 364, lower leaf). translation.original_ref: RV 5.46.2-5 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 2, varga 28); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 364v
translation.original_text:
2agna̱ indra̱ varu̍ṇa̱ mitra̱ devā̱ḥ śardha̱ḥ pra ya̍nta̱ māru̍to̱ta vi̍ṣṇo | u̱bhā nāsa̍tyā ru̱dro adha̱ gnāḥ pū̱ṣā bhaga̱ḥ sara̍svatī juṣanta ||
3i̱ndrā̱gnī mi̱trāvaru̱ṇādi̍ti̱ṁ sva̍ḥ pṛthi̱vīṁ dyām ma̱ruta̱ḥ parva̍tām̐ a̱paḥ | hu̱ve viṣṇu̍m pū̱ṣaṇa̱m brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̱m bhaga̱ṁ nu śaṁsa̍ṁ savi̱tāra̍m ū̱taye̍ ||
4u̱ta no̱ viṣṇu̍r u̱ta vāto̍ a̱sridho̍ draviṇo̱dā u̱ta somo̱ maya̍s karat | u̱ta ṛ̱bhava̍ u̱ta rā̱ye no̍ a̱śvino̱ta tvaṣṭo̱ta vibhvānu̍ maṁsate ||
5u̱ta tyan no̱ māru̍ta̱ṁ śardha̱ ā ga̍mad divikṣa̱yaṁ ya̍ja̱tam ba̱rhir ā̱sade̍ | bṛha̱spati̱ḥ śarma̍ pū̱ṣota no̍ yamad varū̱thya1̱̍ṁ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā ||
translation.text:
2O Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, and Mitra, give, O ye Gods, and Marut host, and Vishṇu. May both Nâsatyas, Rudra, heavenly Matrons, Pûshan, Sarasvatî, Bhaga, accept us.
3Indra and Agni, Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the Waters, Mountains, Maruts, Sky, and Earth and Heaven, Vishṇu I call, Pûshan, and Brahmaṇaspati, and Bhaga, Ṣaṅsa, Savitar that they may help.
4May Vishṇu also and Vâta who injures none, and Soma granter of possessions give us joy; And may the R̥ibhus and the Aṣvins, Tvashṭar and Vibhvan remember us so that we may have wealth.
5So may the band of Maruts dwelling in the sky, the holy, come to us to sit on sacred grass; Br̥ihaspati and Pûshan grant us sure defence, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman guard and shelter us.

translation.original_ref: RV 5.46.6-8 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 2, varga 28); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 365r
translation.original_text:
6u̱ta tye na̱ḥ parva̍tāsaḥ suśa̱staya̍ḥ sudī̱tayo̍ na̱dya1̱̍s trāma̍ṇe bhuvan | bhago̍ vibha̱ktā śava̱sāva̱sā ga̍mad uru̱vyacā̱ adi̍tiḥ śrotu me̱ hava̍m ||
7de̱vānā̱m patnī̍r uśa̱tīr a̍vantu na̱ḥ prāva̍ntu nas tu̱jaye̱ vāja̍sātaye | yāḥ pārthi̍vāso̱ yā a̱pām api̍ vra̱te tā no̍ devīḥ suhavā̱ḥ śarma̍ yacchata ||
8u̱ta gnā vya̍ntu de̱vapa̍tnīr indrā̱ṇy a1̱̍gnāyy a̱śvinī̱ rāṭ | ā roda̍sī varuṇā̱nī śṛ̍ṇotu̱ vyantu̍ de̱vīr ya ṛ̱tur janī̍nām ||
translation.text:
6And may the Mountains famed in noble eulogies, and the fair-gleaming Rivers keep us safe from harm. May Bhaga the Dispenser come with power and grace, and far-pervading Aditi listen to my call.
7May the Gods' Spouses aid us of their own freewill, aid us to offspring and the winning of the spoil. Grant us protection, O ye gracious Goddesses, ye who are on the earth or in the waters' realm.
8May the Dames, wives of Gods, enjoy our presents, Râṭ, Aṣvinî, Agnâyî, and Indrâṇî. May Rodasî and Varuṇânî hear us, and Goddesses come at the Matrons' season.
